Tuberous sclerosis is an autosomal dominant genetic disease that causes the growth of tumors in the brain and many other organs, including the kidneys, heart, lungs, eyes, liver, pancreas, spleen, and skin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular pathogenesis of TSC.
the development of novel methods for the detection of mutations in the TSC1 and Tsc2 genes, which cause tuberous sclerosis.
the development of new methods of diagnosis and therapy of TSC, and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of TSC pathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TSC is a genetic disorder that is caused by mutations in the TSC1 and Tsc2 genes.
TSC is a disease that is associated with the development of hamartomas in many organs, but particularly in the skin, brain and kidney.
TSC1 and Tsc2 are tumor suppressor genes.
